instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in Gildas’ record of the Britons’ defence.
instruction.sound: Fill in the gaps in Gildasses record of the Britons’ defence.

atoms.b: To stop the ((++invaders supporters)), the different kingdoms in ((++Britain Rome)) needed to work together.
They united under one ((++leader loser)) called Ambrosius Aurelianus, and they fought back against the ((++Saxons Britons)), Angles and Jutes.

instruction.text: Let’s check the reliability of what Gildas wrote by looking at another source. Find the copy of The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle on the bookshelf.
instruction.sound: Let’s check the reliability of what Gildass wrote by looking at another source. Find the copy of The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle on the bookshelf.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the question.

atoms.text: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle agrees that the Britons united under one leader. This text was written from a Saxon perspective, whereas Gildas wrote from a Briton’s perspective.

atoms.a: What do you think it means if two sources from different perspectives agree on something?

atoms.b: In around AD 500, Ambrosius Aurelianus won a great ((++victory defeat)) for the Britons at the Battle of Badon.
However, ((++archaeologists astronomers)) have found very little physical ((++evidence education)), so we don’t know exactly where the battle was fought.

feedback.end: The famous legend of King Arthur is likely based on these historical events. Ambrosius even appears as Arthur’s uncle in some versions of the story.

instruction.text: Drag the equipment into the soldier’s hands to prepare him for battle.

text: In an Anglo-Saxon battle, soldiers would lock their shields together to make a shield wall.

instruction.text: Here is a map of Britain in AD 550. Select the Britons label to learn more.

feedback.end: The Britons’ fight back was not enough to keep out the invaders. By now, most of Eastern England was controlled by Germanic tribes.

atoms.b: The Saxons, Angles and Jutes gradually mixed together to ((++become upset)) the Anglo-Saxons. They would go on to change ((++Britain Egypt)) forever.
